catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 2 topline results meeting endpoints
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive top-line results were reported from the Phase 2 portion of a Phase 1/2 trial of ABCL635 in postmenopausal women with moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms. The study met primary endpoints with statistically significant reductions in hot flash frequency and severity after a single subcutaneous dose and showed improvements in sleep and PGI-C, supporting potential best-in-class efficacy.
catalyst_text_evidence: AbCellera (NASDAQ:ABCL) today announced positive top-line results from the Phase 2 portion of its Phase 1/2 clinical trial evaluating ABCL635, an investigational neurokinin 3 receptor (NK3R) antagonist antibody. The study met the primary efficacy endpoints achieving statistically significant reductions in both frequency and severity of VMSM-S at week 4 compared to placebo after a single dose. ABCL635 was also observed to significantly improve sleep and patient global impression of change (PGI-C).

catalyst_text: Announced positive interim Phase 1 clinical results
detailed_catalyst_text: Interim Phase 1 data in healthy volunteers showed favorable tolerability with no serious adverse events or liver enzyme elevations, and a pharmacokinetic half-life of about 24 days supporting monthly dosing. Biomarkers showed sustained, dose-dependent suppression of testosterone indicating NK3R target engagement, and the program has progressed into a Phase 2 efficacy study in postmenopausal women with moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms.
catalyst_text_evidence: AbCellera (NASDAQ:ABCL) today announced financial results for the first quarter of 2026 and positive interim results from the Phase 1 portion of its ongoing Phase 1/2 clinical trial of ABCL635. A favorable tolerability profile: ABCL635 was well-tolerated across all doses, with no serious adverse events or elevations in liver enzymes. Treatment-emergent adverse events were generally mild and transient. A pharmacokinetic profile that supports monthly dosing: ABCL635 exhibited an estimated half-life of ~24 days, supporting the potential for a once monthly subcutaneous dose. Strong suppression of biomarkers of target engagement: To confirm target engagement of NK3R on kisspeptin, neurokinin B, and dynorphin (KNDy) neurons in the infundibular nucleus of the hypothalamus, testosterone, a clinically validated surrogate biomarker of NK3R antagonism, was measured in male volunteers. ABCL635 demonstrated sustained and dose-dependent suppression of testosterone over a four-week period. Based on these data, AbCellera advanced ABCL635 into a Phase 2 study, as announced earlier this year. The Phase 2 is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with approximately 80 postmenopausal women designed to evaluate the efficacy of ABCL635 in reducing the frequency and severity of moderate-to-severe VMS.

catalyst_text: First patients dosed in Phase 2 randomized study
detailed_catalyst_text: First patients were dosed in the Phase 2 portion of an ongoing Phase 1/2 clinical trial evaluating an antibody for moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms associated with menopause. This advances the program into a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled proof-of-concept study in approximately 80 postmenopausal women, an important step toward establishing efficacy.
catalyst_text_evidence: “AbCellera (NASDAQ:ABCL) today announced that the first patients have been dosed in the Phase 2 portion of its ongoing Phase 1/2 clinical trial for ABCL635.” “ABCL635 is a potential first-in-class non-hormonal treatment for moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms (VMS) associated with menopause.” “The Phase 2 portion is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study designed to evaluate the efficacy of ABCL635 in reducing the frequency and severity of VMS in 80 postmenopausal women.”
